issue: Lessor (sales-type lease) content sits in the FAR lessee module, is not marked optional, and is never taught in the lesson. Lessor accounting moved to BAR under CPA Evolution and is still BAR in the 2026 Blueprint; FAR Area III.F is "Lessee accounting" only. These items count toward FAR practice, mixed sets and readiness.
evidence: far-lsf-14 (selling profit timing), far-lsf-27 (FV 400,000 - carrying 300,000 = 100,000 selling profit), far-lsf-28 (lessor IDC expensed when FV != carrying amount) and the TBS (payment 400,000/4.3121 = 92,762; NIL 331,817; Dr NIL/Cr Sales, Dr COGS/Cr Inventory) are all lessor accounting under ASC 842-30. The keys are technically correct. The lesson (unit title "Leases (Lessee)") has no lessor section. Repo docs/BLUEPRINT_NOTES.md says lessor accounting is "not built as FAR content"; review/reference/far-standards.md 1c and blueprint-notes.md list lessor accounting as BAR. Mcq.optional exists in the schema; the TBS schema has no optional flag, so the TBS cannot be excluded except by moving it.
source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints 2026, FAR Area III.F (Lessee accounting); BAR Area II; review/reference/far-standards.md 1c
fix: Set optional: true on far-lsf-14, -27 and -28 (or move them to a BAR bank). Remove far-tbs-r3-sales-type-lease from the FAR TBS pool (move it to BAR content), or add a TBS-level optional flag to schema.ts/build.ts and set it. If any of them stay, add a short "lessor view (BAR)" note to the lesson.

issue: The stem asks for the "initial lease liability" when the first payment is made at commencement. ASC 842-20-30-1 measures the lease liability at the PV of lease payments NOT YET PAID, so distractor (d) $133,651 is defensible. The item explanation ("present value of the remaining lease payments at commencement") actually describes (d), which contradicts the key (b), and choice (d)'s rationale ("The first payment is part of the liability") contradicts the item explanation.
evidence: 50,000 x 3.67301 = 183,651 (PV of all 4 payments, the key). Payment 1 is made at commencement, so the PV of the unpaid payments = 183,651 - 50,000 = 133,651 (= 50,000 x 2.67301). The ROU asset = 133,651 + 50,000 paid at commencement = 183,651 either way. far-x3-10 avoids the problem by saying "(before the first payment)"; far-lsf-12 does not.
fix: Add "(before the first payment)" to the stem, as in far-x3-10, or ask for "the present value of the lease payments". Rewrite the explanation: "50,000 x 3.67301 = 183,651, the PV of all four payments including the one due at commencement; the day-1 payment immediately reduces the liability to 133,651." Change (d)'s rationale to "That is the balance after the commencement-date payment."

issue: Skill is mislabeled by two levels: a pure recall question (how a sales-type lessor treats initial direct costs) is labeled "analysis" with difficulty 3.
evidence: The stem asks for one remembered rule (IDC are expensed at commencement when FV != carrying amount) with no facts to analyze or compute. Under the Blueprint, recalling a rule is Remembering & Understanding. Mislabels move the module's skill-mix counts that the Blueprint targets depend on.
fix: If the item is kept (see the lessor-scope finding), relabel it skill: remembering, difficulty: 1 or 2.

issue: Skill and difficulty labels are off by one level across the module. One-step application computations in the far-lsf-16 to -27 block are labeled analysis/difficulty 3. Identical twin items carry different labels. Two conceptual-recall items are labeled application.
evidence: Each "analysis" item needs one rule and one or two arithmetic steps: lsf-21 379,079 x 10% = 37,908; lsf-18 100,000 - 37,908 = 62,092; lsf-22 379,079 + 37,908 - 100,000 = 316,987; lsf-23 75,816 + 37,908 = 113,724; lsf-24 6/8 = 75%; lsf-25 (416,987 - 100,000) x 10% = 31,699; lsf-27 400,000 - 300,000. Twins: lsf-05 (150,000/8) is application/2 but lsf-16 (400,000/8, same facts) is analysis/3; lsf-09 is application/2 but lsf-26 (identical 20,000/15,000 facts) is analysis/3; lsf-03 is difficulty 2 but lsf-13 (same formula) is difficulty 3. lsf-11 (expense pattern) and lsf-14 (when selling profit is recognized) are conceptual recall. Label distribution as keyed (practice+exam): application 17, analysis 11, remembering 3; after correction, about application 23-24, remembering 6, analysis 1-2.
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprints, skill definitions (FAR: R&U 5-15%, Application 45-55%, Analysis 35-45%)
fix: Relabel lsf-16, -18, -21, -22, -23, -24, -26 and -27 as application, difficulty 2 (lsf-25 application, difficulty 3). Set lsf-13 to difficulty 2. Relabel lsf-11 and lsf-14 as remembering. If the module needs analysis-level items, write real ones (for example, compare finance and operating effects on the statements, or classify with interacting criteria) rather than relabeling.

issue: Distractor rationales name the wrong error, or none, for the number they model.
evidence: Recomputed: lsf-05 (c) 21,429 = 150,000/7, but the rationale says "averaging the two periods" (average of 5 and 8 = 6.5 gives 23,077). lsf-16 (c) 40,000 = 400,000/10: no plausible error gives 10, and the rationale "Divide by the 8-year life" names none. lsf-18 (c) 75,816 = 379,079/5, straight-line principal (the ROU amortization); the rationale "Use the effective interest" doesn't say so. lsf-21 (d) 62,092 = principal reduction (100,000 - 37,908); rationale "Not the computation." lsf-22 (c) 303,263 = 379,079 - 75,816 (subtracts ROU amortization from the liability); rationale "Not the computation." lsf-26 (c) 15,000 = the expected residual value; rationale "Not the amount."
fix: lsf-05 (c): use 23,077 (150,000/6.5) to keep the "averaging" rationale, or explain 21,429 differently. lsf-16 (c): replace 40,000 with a modeled error (e.g., 57,143 = 400,000/7 for 8 - 1 years), or drop it. Rewrite the others: lsf-18 (c) "Reduces principal straight-line (379,079/5); principal reduction is payment minus interest." lsf-21 (d) "That is the principal portion of the payment, not interest." lsf-22 (c) "That subtracts ROU amortization; amortization reduces the asset, not the liability." lsf-26 (c) "That is the expected residual value; the lessee includes only the 5,000 shortfall."

issue: Item-level explanations state the rule without the computation. Some are close to circular (e.g., "The liability grows by interest and falls by payments."). The standard requires the item explanation to show the computation for calculation items.
evidence: lsf-13: formula only (needs 183,651 + 3,000 - 5,000 = 181,651). lsf-16: rule only (needs 400,000/8 = 50,000). lsf-21: "liability balance times the discount rate" (needs 379,079 x 10% = 37,908). lsf-22: rule only (379,079 + 37,908 - 100,000 = 316,987). lsf-23: no numbers. lsf-25: no numbers ((416,987 - 100,000) x 10% = 31,699). lsf-26: no numbers (20,000 - 15,000). lsf-27: no numbers (400,000 - 300,000; revenue 400,000 and COGS 300,000 for a dealer). The computations appear only in the correct-choice text, if at all.
fix: Add the full computation (with rule citation, e.g., ASC 842-20-35-8 for amortization, 842-20-35-1 for interest) to each item explanation, as far-lsf-02/-03/-05/-07 already do.

issue: Trap labels don't match the misconception the distractor models, and the same error is labeled differently from item to item.
evidence: chk2 (a) operating activities = classification error, labeled partial-computation (no computation). lsf-12 (c) 200,000 undiscounted, labeled partial-computation, while lsf-02 (a) labels the same error wrong-rule. x3-10 (b) 250,000 undiscounted, labeled partial-computation. lsf-17 (b) "disclosed only", labeled partial-computation. lsf-21 (d) 62,092 = principal mistaken for interest, labeled distractor-number, while lsf-18 (b) labels the inverse confusion "reversed".
fix: Change chk2 (a) to wrong-classification; lsf-12 (c), x3-10 (b) and lsf-17 (b) to wrong-rule; lsf-21 (d) to reversed.

issue: Near-duplicate items in the practice pool test the same fact the same way.
evidence: lsf-26 repeats lsf-09 exactly: guarantee 20,000, expected residual 15,000, answer 5,000, same four values reordered. lsf-16 repeats lsf-05: ownership transfers, 5-year term, 8-year life, ROU/8. lsf-13 repeats lsf-03: ROU = liability + IDC - incentive, with the IDC and incentive amounts swapped. Flashcards fc3, fc5 and fc7 also drill these facts. The cue scanner missed them because the wording differs.
fix: Replace lsf-26 with an RVG variant: expected residual at or above the guarantee, so 0 is included, or the RVG pushes the PV test over 90%. Replace lsf-16 with a purchase-option-reasonably-certain case, or a case where useful life is shorter than the term. Replace lsf-13 with an ROU computation that includes a payment made at commencement (ties to lsf-12).

issue: A four-item chain on the same 379,079 lease leaks answers between items, and one stem depends on order ("Using the finance lease above"), which breaks when practice is shuffled.
evidence: lsf-21 asks for year-1 interest (key 37,908). The lsf-22 and lsf-23 stems both state "$37,908 interest", and lsf-18's correct-choice rationale prints it. lsf-18 and lsf-21 use the same four values (100,000; 37,908; 75,816; 62,092), so each item's key is a distractor in the other. The lsf-22 stem begins "Using the finance lease above".
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 6 (one item revealing the answer to another)
fix: Make each stem self-contained with its own numbers (e.g., vary payment and rate per item), remove "above", and don't give one item's key as a stem fact in another.

issue: Answer cues: in each item the key is the longest option and the only one that echoes the standard's qualifying language. Some distractors are implausible.
evidence: lsf-01: key (b), 86 characters, is the only option with "reasonably certain" (the criterion wording); distractors run 44-58 characters. lsf-15: key "A risk-free rate, by class of asset" is the longest and the only qualified option; distractors (c) "The rate on its savings account" and (d) "Any rate it chooses" are not credible (cues.md flags both items).
fix: lsf-01: shorten the key ("A purchase option the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise") and lengthen the distractors (e.g., "A renewal option at market rates that the lessee may exercise"). lsf-15: use plausible distractors such as "A risk-free rate, applied entity-wide to all leases", "The lessee's weighted-average cost of capital" and "The rate implicit in the lease, estimated from the lessor's pricing".

issue: This mock-exam item copies the lesson's worked example (same payment, rate, term, timing and answer), so it tests recall of a number the learner has already seen. The item is also used in both far-mock-1 and far-mock-2.
evidence: Lesson worked example: $50,000 due each January 1, 5 years, 6%, annuity due, 4.46511, giving 223,255, and 173,255 after the first payment. far-x3-10: $50,000 at the beginning of each year, 5 years, 6%, 4.4651; key 223,255, distractor 173,255. The mock JSON lists far-x3-10 in both far-mock-1.json and far-mock-2.json.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 7 and check 8 (realism)
fix: Change the exam item's facts (e.g., $64,000, 7%, 4 years; factors given), and use it on only one mock form.

issue: The lesson body never teaches three things the items test: (1) how the lease term is determined (renewal and termination options reasonably certain of exercise); (2) the components of the ROU asset (IDC, incentives, payments made at or before commencement), which appear only in keyTakeaways and in no worked example; (3) that the non-PBE risk-free election is made by class of underlying asset.
evidence: (1) x3-12 (d) and Lease B of the u11 TBS ("Renewal at market rates, not reasonably certain") need the lease-term rule; the lesson and Leases II never define lease term (grep "lease term" finds only the amortization and short-term lines). (2) lsf-03, lsf-13 and x3 TBS rows r and je (135,484 = 132,484 + 3,000 IDC) test the ROU build-up; the body's "Measuring at commencement" covers only lease payments and the discount rate. (3) The lesson says "private companies may elect a risk-free rate"; the lsf-15 key adds "by class of asset" (ASU 2021-09).
source: ASC 842-10-30-1 (lease term); ASC 842-20-30-5 (ROU asset); ASC 842-20-30-3 as amended by ASU 2021-09
fix: Add a short "Lease term" paragraph (noncancellable period plus periods covered by renewal options reasonably certain to be exercised and termination options reasonably certain not to be exercised). Add an "ROU asset" paragraph with a two-line example including IDC and an incentive. Revise the discount-rate note to: "lessees that are not PBEs (including most NFPs) may elect a risk-free rate by class of underlying asset; the implicit rate must still be used when readily determinable".

issue: The big idea says classification "only changes how the cost shows up on the income statement". That is an overstatement: classification also changes cash-flow classification, balance-sheet line items and the ROU asset's carrying amount after commencement.
evidence: The lesson's own Presentation section says finance-lease principal is financing; operating-lease payments are operating (Leases II takeaway). ASC 842-20-45-1 requires finance and operating ROU assets and liabilities to be presented in separate line items. The Leases II table, on the same facts, shows an ROU asset at 12/31 of 183,650 (operating) vs 178,604 (finance).
fix: Say "classification mainly changes the income-statement pattern (one straight-line cost vs. front-loaded interest plus amortization), and also the cash-flow classification and later ROU asset balances".

issue: The rationales use "executory costs", an ASC 840 term that ASC 842 no longer uses.
evidence: lsf-01 (c): "Executory cost arrangements don't affect classification." x3-12 (a): "Executory costs do not affect classification." ASC 842 treats lessee-paid property taxes and insurance as payments that are not separate components of the contract (842-10-15-30(b)) or as variable payments. The conclusion (no effect on classification) is correct.
fix: Reword: "Who pays property taxes, insurance or maintenance isn't one of the five classification criteria."

issue: Row k2 omits the PV/"substantially all" criterion from its options, and the exhibit gives neither the fair value nor a statement that the asset is standard, so two criteria can't be ruled out from the facts. 25 minutes is generous for 2 dropdowns, 5 numerics and a 3-line JE (u11, which needs more work, gets 20). The TBS also appears on both far-mock-1 and far-mock-2.
evidence: k2 options: ownership, purchase option, major part, specialized; PV >= substantially all is missing. Instructions: "no transfer of ownership or purchase option"; no fair value and no statement on specialization. All keys recomputed and correct: 132,484; 135,484; 10,599; 103,083; 33,871; JE balances (135,484 = 132,484 + 3,000).
fix: Add a fair value (e.g., $165,000, so PV is 80% and fails the 90% test) and "standard equipment with alternative uses" to the instructions, add the PV option to k2, cut minutes to about 18-20, and use the TBS on one mock form only.

issue: For annuity-due leases, the lesson and TBS label one figure "lease liability and ROU asset at commencement". Under ASC 842 the liability is the PV of unpaid payments, so it already excludes the day-1 payment. This blurs the distinction behind the far-lsf-12 ambiguity.
evidence: Lesson worked step 1: "Lease liability and ROU asset at commencement = 223,255". The JE then credits Lease liability 173,255 (memo reconciles). u11 row l0: "Lease liability / ROU asset at commencement = 434,918"; the strict liability after the Jan 1 payment = 434,918 - 120,000 = 314,918, while the ROU = 434,918. The keys are not wrong: a learner reading "ROU asset" enters 434,918.
fix: Lesson: label step 1 "PV of all payments = ROU asset 223,255; lease liability after the day-1 payment = 173,255 (PV of the unpaid payments)". u11: relabel l0 "ROU asset at commencement (PV of all four payments)".
